title: AI & Automation
description: Configure AI Brain, qualifying conversations, knowledge, automated follow-up and Insights.

pages.title: AI Brain and Playbook
pages.summary: Configure the source of truth for SHVYA's organization-specific AI behavior.
pages.body:
## What AI Brain controls
AI Brain combines your About/company information, supported Bot Languages, one saved AI Playbook, approved FAQs, indexed knowledge sources and organization-specific configuration. It is not a separately trainable model or a second contact database.

## Prepare an effective Playbook
Open the Dashboard's AI Brain / AI Setup workspace. Configure the following named sections with your own accurate business information:

- **Rules:** persona, language, allowed claims, policy and handoff.
- **Welcome Message:** appropriate greeting and first-step intent.
- **Qualification Questions:** only the ordered questions the AI should ask in New Lead.
- **Acknowledgment Message:** how to acknowledge a customer's answer.
- **Qualification Criteria:** conditions that must be true before a lead is qualified.
- **Stage shifting logic:** allowable destinations and their conditions.
- **Attribute mapping logic:** which evidence maps to which exact CRM field.
- **Reminder creation logic:** when the AI should propose a follow-up reminder.

## Recommended setup
1. Save your About description and approved languages.
2. Write explicit questions and accepted answers/options.
3. Map to already-created CRM attributes with their valid types.
4. Add FAQs and knowledge sources; verify uploaded processing finished.
5. Test sample customer questions, unclear answers, stage transitions and file sharing in **AI Sandbox**.
6. Enable authorized AI controls and verify one live test conversation.

## Download saved AI Brain
The **Download saved AI Brain** action generates a versioned JSON snapshot of your currently saved configuration. It is useful for review, backup comparison, audit or describing an organization setup. **Downloading or editing that JSON does not automatically change live SHVYA AI.** Save changes in the supported Dashboard screens.

## Important limitations
AI decisions cannot invent CRM state. Backend validation owns attributes, reminders and stage transitions. The model should use verified About, FAQ and processed knowledge content for factual claims; a URL entered without processing is not the same as live web browsing.

[Qualification](/docs/ai-automation/qualification/) · [Knowledge](/docs/ai-automation/knowledge-sources/).

pages.title: AI lead qualification
pages.summary: Ask configured questions, capture answers and move a lead only after the criteria are met.
pages.body:
## Define the qualification journey
Qualification runs in the designated New Lead stage. Create a clear, ordered list of questions in the Playbook and map important answers to CRM attributes. Write criteria separately; answering all questions does not necessarily satisfy a business requirement.

## How a conversation should behave
1. Respond to the customer's actual question first.
2. Identify which qualification questions already have valid, customer-supplied answers.
3. Acknowledge useful input and ask the next unresolved configured question.
4. Save only validated values to existing, correctly typed organization attributes.
5. When required criteria are met, request the configured stage transition through backend validation.
6. In subsequent stages, use sales-support behavior rather than repeating already-answered New Lead questions.

## Build robust question mappings
Use recognizable answers and synonyms, including option letters where relevant. Define how ambiguous statements should be clarified and what counts as a complete answer. Avoid treating the AI's own previous text or a template message as customer evidence.

## Example
Question: **Where do you currently manage new leads?** Options: WhatsApp, Excel/Sheets or CRM. Map an answer such as “we use spreadsheets” to the exact accepted **Lead Management Tool** value.

## Verify end to end
Test multi-answer messages, off-topic questions, short replies, code-switching between allowed languages and incomplete requirements in Sandbox. Then inspect a real test lead: the expected attributes should be stored and the stage should move at most once when the configured criteria are satisfied.

[AI Brain](/docs/ai-automation/ai-brain/) · [Stage shifting](/docs/ai-automation/stage-shifting/).

pages.title: Stage shifting and CRM actions
pages.summary: Understand AI-authorized moves, attribute saving and reminder creation.
pages.body:
## Action authority
An AI output may propose an action; SHVYA's backend checks the lead, pipeline, stage, organization, attribute definitions and policy before making any change. Generated text such as “You're qualified” does not prove a corresponding database transition.

## Stage move setup
1. Create a valid destination stage inside the intended pipeline.
2. Give it a descriptive purpose and define any required attributes.
3. In AI Brain, specify exactly when the lead should enter that stage.
4. Use Sandbox to test both passing and failing conditions.
5. Confirm the saved CRM state in a live, authorized test lead.

## Attribute writes
Use exact active field names and valid option values. Evidence must come from the customer's conversation; unknown or contradictory data should be clarified, not guessed.

## Reminders and appointments
A request such as “call me tomorrow at 3 PM” can produce a reminder when the timestamp and timezone are sufficiently clear and the permitted action succeeds. An appointment requires SHVYA Calendar availability validation; a reminder alone must never be described as a reserved slot.

## If it looks successful only in chat
Inspect the lead's CRM record and AI Trace action receipt. Look for rejection reasons including wrong pipeline, missing required attributes, insufficient evidence, inactive stage or disabled AI. Adjust the configured rules, not the tenant guardrails.

[CRM routing](/docs/crm-leads/pipelines-stages/) · [Reminders](/docs/crm-leads/reminders-calls/).

pages.title: Knowledge sources and FAQs
pages.summary: Give AI reliable, organization-approved evidence instead of unsupported answers.
pages.body:
## Knowledge types
SHVYA supports company About information, separate FAQs, configured website URLs and readable uploaded documents. Supported source-file types include PDF, DOCX, TXT, CSV and XLSX. The system extracts/indexes approved source content for retrieval with PostgreSQL pgvector and keyword matching.

## Add a source
1. Open AI Brain / Knowledge Sources.
2. Add an approved webpage URL or upload a supported readable file.
3. Save and wait for the source processing/indexing status to show readiness.
4. Ask targeted factual questions in AI Sandbox and check the answer against the actual source.
5. Replace or disable obsolete pricing documents and FAQs before production use.

## What indexed means
Adding a website URL does not mean the AI visits the live website on every reply. It can use the extracted, processed content available to the organization. A webpage that blocks fetching, a damaged upload or unreadable scan may not yield usable evidence. Scanned documents may require OCR and quality checks.

## Write high-quality FAQs
Add one realistic customer question and a precise, approved answer at a time. Include constraints, validity and exceptions rather than just marketing claims. FAQs are factual evidence, not hidden qualification questions.

## When the AI says it cannot answer
Confirm the source is active, current and processed, that the answer is truly included, and that the customer phrased a related question. Read the relevant AI Trace before declaring the model broken. Do not add unsupported product claims to force an answer.

[AI Brain](/docs/ai-automation/ai-brain/) · [Knowledge troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/ai-not-replying/).

pages.title: AI-Guided File Sharing
pages.summary: Send approved brochures or other files only when their sharing conditions are satisfied.
pages.body:
## Why this is separate from knowledge
A file can be stored so that SHVYA is allowed to share it; successful file delivery does not prove its text was indexed for answering questions. Likewise, an indexed internal document is not automatically approved for customer delivery.

## Configure a shareable file
1. Upload the organization's current file to AI Brain's supported file area.
2. Mark the file as eligible for customer sharing where the UI requires it.
3. Write a precise **When and why to send** instruction: such as with the approved welcome message, after interest in a service, or upon an explicit brochure request.
4. Save and test the rule in AI Sandbox, including cases where the file must **not** be sent.
5. Verify one live authorized delivery on each channel you intend to use.

## Channel behavior
Meta WhatsApp Cloud API/Coexistence and Hosted use their channel-specific attachment senders. Instagram may deliver supported PDFs as native attachments and other types using authorized links. A download link may expire and requires eligible access.

## Troubleshoot a missing brochure
Check all five stages: file exists; sharing is permitted; current version is ready; the customer message meets the condition; and the provider has acknowledged actual send. Re-open the saved instruction and AI Trace. If no send occurred, the bot must not claim it attached the file.

## Safety
Only organization-owned eligible files may be shared. Do not attach private pricing, credentials or internal SOPs to a public welcome message.

[AI Sandbox](/docs/ai-automation/ai-sandbox/) · [Message delivery](/docs/messaging-channels/whatsapp-inbox/).

pages.title: AI Sandbox testing
pages.summary: Simulate lead conversations and inspect decisions without sending customer messages.
pages.body:
## What Sandbox is
AI Sandbox runs a preview of the configured AI conversation and supported CRM actions. Its simulated lead, selected stage, conversation history and file history are not real customer messages. Stage changes and file cards shown in Sandbox are previews, not proof of live send or database mutation.

## Test a full journey
1. Save the latest AI Brain configuration.
2. Open **AI Sandbox** and choose a starting stage and relevant channel/source.
3. Ask a company FAQ; compare the answer to approved source evidence.
4. Answer the qualification questions, including unexpected phrasing and several answers in one message.
5. Verify the preview records the expected mapped values and only authorized stage moves.
6. Ask for a brochure and confirm the correct file-sharing rule is selected.
7. Restart the chat before running a new independent scenario.

## Include failure cases
Ask a question absent from your knowledge, request a meeting with unclear timing, answer a dropdown with an invalid value, and use different allowed languages. The bot should clarify or decline unsupported assertions rather than invent a booking or action.

## Moving into production
Once a sandbox scenario passes, repeat representative cases from a disposable authorized test contact in a live WhatsApp or Instagram account. Real provider permissions, number routing, worker scheduling, credits and outbound acknowledgements are not proved by Sandbox.

[Live testing checklist](/docs/getting-started/launch-checklist/) · [AI troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/ai-not-replying/).

pages.title: Cadence: follow-up sequences
pages.summary: Build reply-aware scheduled follow-ups and choose the correct channel.
pages.body:
## Purpose
Cadence sequences define how and when SHVYA follows up with a lead. Steps may use supported channel messages, connected email or reminder actions depending on configuration. The schedule is stored as durable state, and worker dispatch rechecks current permissions.

## Create a sequence
1. Open [Cadence](/dashboard/cadence/) and create a sequence.
2. Select the lead segment, target pipeline and available outbound channel.
3. Add messages/reminder steps in the intended order with reasonable intervals.
4. Choose the appropriate sender, template or connected email identity.
5. Configure response-aware delay and stopping conditions.
6. Test on a disposable lead and inspect the step history before assigning a larger audience.

## Important guardrails
A reply can defer follow-up depending on settings. Disabling the lead's follow-up control should prevent eligible future auto follow-ups. API messages sent after the WhatsApp customer-service window closes require approved templates; a timer does not override provider policy.

## Diagnose a missing send
Check the assigned sequence, lead follow-up state, due time, customer reply activity, connected provider, current pipeline sender, template status and automation worker/queue. A scheduled step is not identical to a delivered message.

[Workflows](/docs/ai-automation/workflows/) · [WhatsApp rules](/docs/messaging-channels/delivery-windows/).

pages.title: Workflows: events and actions
pages.summary: Automate validated CRM changes and messages using configured triggers.
pages.body:
## What a Workflow does
A Workflow combines an event, matching conditions and one or more permitted actions. It uses the current CRM state rather than treating a UI rule as unlimited authority.

## Supported trigger families
Stage moved; sequence ended; lead created; no response; keyword; stage idle; manually logged call. Conditions can include pipeline, stage, fixed lead Source and eligible attributes.

## Supported action families
Start/stop Cadence, move a stage, schedule a WhatsApp message, send a connected-email message, set a reminder, update an attribute, change lead AI and change lead follow-up controls.

## Create your first rule
1. Open [Workflows](/dashboard/workflows/).
2. Select the relevant trigger and set the intended pipeline, stage and source conditions.
3. Add only the action required for the customer journey.
4. Preview/validate the saved rule and test on one disposable lead.
5. Enable it after confirming history and actual state changes.

## Reliability and sending
Long-running or delayed actions are subject to fresh tenant, account, sender, permission and time-window validation at execution. A disabled workflow should not deliver future unauthorized work. Provider uncertainty must not be resolved through unconditional retries.

## Common mistakes
- Sending after a 24-hour Meta window using free-form text.
- Setting a destination stage outside the selected pipeline.
- Configuring a “sequence ends” trigger without selecting the intended sequence.
- Expecting an action while the rule is disabled or a condition does not match.

[Cadence](/docs/ai-automation/cadence/) · [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/first-checks/).

pages.title: Insights and performance
pages.summary: Review funnel progression, campaigns and connection outcomes.
pages.body:
## What to measure
- Time from lead capture to first authorized response.
- Qualification completion and stage conversion for each pipeline.
- Follow-up activity and open or missed actions.
- WhatsApp template/campaign attempted, sent, failed, delivered and read outcomes where provider status exists.
- Relevant channel health or error rates when surfaced by your plan.

## Use Insights
1. Open [Insights](/dashboard/insights/).
2. Select the correct organization scope and any available pipeline/date filters.
3. Compare lead counts and stage movements before changing automation rules.
4. Drill into campaign recipient activity or failed sends where available.
5. Verify the underlying lead or message record before escalating an apparent mismatch.

## Interpret numbers correctly
A **sent** status is not guaranteed delivery, and a conversation classified as **qualified** is not necessarily a closed sale. Provider read receipts may be unavailable. Conversion definitions differ between leads, calls, booked appointments and paid invoices.

## Improve one bottleneck
Select a measurable problem, adjust one Playbook/Cadence/Workflow factor, test on a controlled subset and observe subsequent changes. Avoid inferring revenue growth directly from template read rates.

[CRM overview](/docs/crm-leads/overview/) · [Bulk Campaigns](/docs/messaging-channels/bulk-campaigns/).

pages.title: AI credits, language and control switches
pages.summary: Understand why AI may not run even when a channel is connected.
pages.body:
## AI send requirements
A live automatic response depends on several independent controls: active organization, applicable automation AI toggle, pipeline/stage/lead settings, eligible channel/account, available SHVYA AI credits, permitted sender and running workers. Superadmin policy can impose further limits.

## Configure languages
Save allowed **Bot Languages** in AI Brain and write conditional language behavior in Playbook Rules if needed. Test normal customer language, mixed-language replies and unsupported languages. A language rule cannot make an unapproved claim accurate.

## Model configuration
Qualification, sales-support and post-turn summary model selection may be exposed in settings, but platform-controlled model authority and overrides are Superadmin-managed. A post-turn summary does not replace the authoritative qualification rules.

## Why a conversation stops
- AI disabled at the organization, pipeline, stage or lead level.
- The selected sender is not the lead's current pipeline number.
- Credits or platform health are blocking inference.
- Provider account/session is disconnected or temporarily rate limited.
- A customer message is historical rather than a new eligible inbound.
- The channel-specific free-form window is closed and no compliant template path exists.

## Diagnose before changing
Check the relevant AI switches, latest inbound time, credits, connected account and actual AI Trace. A stopped chat can have a channel/worker cause even when Playbook syntax is fine.

[AI troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting/ai-not-replying/) · [WhatsApp inbox](/docs/messaging-channels/whatsapp-inbox/).

pages.title: Quick Replies and Touchpoints
pages.summary: Create reusable approved content for agents without confusing it with AI qualification.
pages.body:
## What they do
Quick Replies are reusable messages or supported content snippets for day-to-day conversation handling. Some internal screens or legacy code call these **Touchpoints**. They are not the same as qualification questions, and saving a Quick Reply does not automatically schedule a Cadence sequence.

## Prepare useful snippets
1. Open the Quick Replies / Touchpoints workspace in your dashboard.
2. Create short, accurate replies for common requests: introduction, pricing enquiry, meeting preparation or human handoff.
3. Replace placeholders only with known customer facts.
4. Keep privacy, opt-in and allowed product claims in mind.
5. Test inserted content in a real authorized conversation before sharing with your team.

## Where automation fits
Use **Cadence** for scheduled sequences and **Workflows** for event-driven actions. Keep the AI Playbook and FAQ answers separate from snippets so the model's operating rules do not become accidental customer-facing copy.

[Cadence](/docs/ai-automation/cadence/) · [AI Brain](/docs/ai-automation/ai-brain/).
